name: Maple Syrup

source.title: CIRAIG — Is maple syrup good for the planet?

name: Honey
land_types_note: Bees forage on land that exists anyway, so the only farmland is the cane sugar fed to hives; its split is used.
sentient_harm_explanation: Honey is made by honey bees kept in managed hives. A hive makes about 19 kg of honey a year worldwide (23 kg in the US), and about 150,000 worker bees live and die in it over that year — summer workers live about six weeks, winter bees a few months. We count every one of those bees as a life spent in production, the same way a layer hen's whole life is counted for eggs, which works out to roughly 7,800 bees per kg of honey worldwide. Each bee has about a million neurons (a chicken has ~220 million), so one bee counts for far less than one chicken, but there are very many of them. Their ~0.15 years each inside the hive also count as time in captivity.

source.title: USDA FoodData Central
source.note: Honey — nutrition: USDA FDC 169640 (SR Legacy 19296) 'Honey' per 100 g: 304 kcal, protein 0.3 g, fiber 0.2 g, sodium 4 mg, carbs 82.4 g, sugars 82.12 g; per gram.

source.title: Wikipedia — List of Animals by Number of Neurons
source.note: Honey — neuron_count: western honey bee worker brain ~960,000 neurons (Wikipedia list of animals by number of neurons); the same value the model uses for bees killed by pesticides.

source.title: apisavoir.ch — Annual balance of a honey bee colony: key figures (bees raised, honey, worker lifespans)
source.note: Honey — weight_kg: a worker honey bee weighs ~0.1 g (80–120 mg); consistent with 25 kg of bees ≈ 250,000 bees per colony-year (source 433) and with the model's pesticide-bee profile.

source.title: FAOSTAT — Crops and Livestock Products (QCL) bulk download: Strawberries (item 544) and Blueberries (item 552), 2019–2024
source.note: Honey — kg honey per bee death (world): 19.3 kg honey per hive-year / 150,000 bees per hive-year = 1.29e-04 kg (≈7,772 bees per kg honey). FAOSTAT QCL, World 2020–2024: 'Natural honey' (item 1182) 1,924.5 / 1,890.7 / 1,943.1 / 1,959.4 / 1,987.5 kt, mean 1,941 kt; 'Bees' (item 1181) hives 98.9 / 100.3 / 100.3 / 100.8 / 101.7 M, mean 100.4 M -> 19.3 kg honey per hive per year. US: 61.1 kt from 2.64 M hives -> 23.1 kg. ~150,000 worker bees live and die in a hive each year: apisavoir.ch (source 433) puts a colony's annual bee production at ~25 kg of bees (~250,000 at 0.1 g) and a queen's output at ~500,000 over 4–5 years (~110,000/yr); 150,000 is taken between the two. Every bee raised in the hive is counted, as agreed — like layer hens, their deaths are part of keeping the colony in production.
